cells.value: General
Physical checks for any damage
All connectors intact with units
All connectors protected with anticorrosion/ vulcanizing tape
Proper routing of all EW cables on mast and all along its route
AC temperature during system operation is maintained at 18–25 °C
Input supply to isolation transformer
Gyro feed point is same as that during installation (not changed)
Check whether all cables/ PCBs inside processor, LRUs are intact/ fitted properly
Blowers are in running condition during system ON
Pinging checks are OK
Air Filters cleaned
Radar pre-trigger, from each onboard radar, connected to radar blanking interface is OK
(I) Power Supply/ Power Supply cards failure

In the ESM rack, air filters of the ESM units are required to be cleaned by removing the front panel air filter screws. Remove the air filter and clean the same using vacuum cleaner/ air gun or shake the dust off the filter using hand. After cleaning it, place the air filters back to its location and refit the air filter cover with its screws.
A UPS is recommended for the whole system (to power up the ESM racks) to ensure smooth system functioning and to isolate the ship power supply fluctuations/ transients/ abrupt power switching.
Check whether the blowers fixed at the rear of the processor units ESM E/J Processor (WOR), C/D Band Processor are in running condition.

Whenever system is switched OFF and needs to be switched ON again, DO NOT IMMEDIATELY SWITCH ON, and wait for 5 minutes. A time gap of at least 5 minute has to be maintained between each switch OFF and switch ON.
(II) Degradation/ Failure in Front End Electronic components
Avoid exposure of system to high RF radiation when at harbor/ during Sea & Action of other near ships.
Ensure usage of limiters in the Gonio section (DFA) to reduce the future damage of the front end electronic components.
(III) Discontinuities/ poor contact in EW cables
Ensure that connectors (RF cables, Control Cables, Power Supply Cables) are intact at all units on mast. Ensure the same at ESM rack top.
Ensure that all the EW cables connectors and unused/ spare connectors on rack top are protected with water resistant tape/ vulcanizing tape to avoid corrosion.
Ensure all cables are properly routed on mast to avoid tread ON/ step ON/ crushing of the cables by ship staff during mast climbing for other maintenance works like painting/ cleaning etc.
Recommended to replace the Radial RF Cable of Radial make with RF cables of Times Microwave.
(IV) Interface issues (radar blanking, LAN connections, Gyro)

Ensure Gyro feed tapping point finalized during the system installation and HATs is not changed or broken. Also, ensure that ship Gyro data is reaching to the input of the interfacing unit by switching on SDN/ Gyro converters as configured for each platform.

Ensure the radar pre-trigger (Pre-Sync) output pulse is reaching the radar blanking junction box (Interface) of the EW System by co-ax cable from the available onboard radars. Make sure that the cable is not broken/ physically damaged/ disturbed. Pre-trigger should meet the following as per MIL 751 A: Pulse Amplitude: 6-28 V across 75 ohm load (Positive Polarity) Pre-trigger Delay: 1μsec (minimum) before Actual Transmission pulse Pulse Width: 1 μsec (minimum)
(V) Failure in digital cards/ circuit

Check for any loose cables out of its position, PCBs Loosening. If found so, ensure proper tightening of loose cables, fix cables into their positions, insert PCBs firmly into their slot by pressing on the facial panel of the PCBs and tighten the PCB fixing screws softly (only 3 to 4 turns of the screw in the clockwise direction is sufficient). DO NOT over tighten the PCB fixing screws.
Inspect the following, wherever applicable:- LEDs in ESM rack LEDs on processor LRUs
Checks Under System Power Off Condition:
Ensure all system units are properly installed as per the installation manual.

Ensure all the antenna radomes of mast mount units DFA (starboard), DFA (port), C/D Antenna and DFS unit, Front End unit, 18-40 RDF units (if installed) are free from dust and foreign deposits/ bodies. These units need to be cleaned with soft damp cloth. CAUTION: DO NOT PAINT RADOMES/ MAST MOUNT UNITS/ CABLES

To ensure that the UPS Batteries do not drain or become dry, switch ON the isolation transformer at least for one hour in a month (especially during ship refits), since the isolation transformer 230 V AC output supplies the power to UPS of Operation Console.
Checks Under System Power On Condition:
Carry out pinging checks with all subunits and wherever applicable
Ensure all OB Spares are available at all times and are functionally OK.
Power ON / maintenance BITE checks Verification of BITE logs
Display of tracks in console containing frequency parameter, PW & PRI for available emissions in harbour
Are threshold level settings as per HATs/ SATs document
Are attenuation levels in C/D band as per HATs/ SATs document
Are offsets in DDT cards appropriate?
(VII) Miscellaneous information (to be sought from ship’s staff)
Average DOA errors and Radar Advantage Factor
Existing known defects, if any
Recurring defects, with implication on system performance
Details of critical modules/ sub-assemblies with high failure rate, warranting augmentation in OBS
